70a9582de1.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and śukraḥ in maghā siṁhaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°29′41.92″.
70a9582de1.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°29′41.92″, 0°29′22.04″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°54′57.31″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.70, elongation 3°59′23.24″ E). śukraḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 1°24′39.24″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 4°07′52.86″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śukraḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

70a9f816db.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈4.4 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
70a9f816db.d: Magnitude: 37% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈4.4 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 03:03►17:34 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
70a9f816db.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

70b6a6e896.b: Event occured on 1736-04-29 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
70b6a6e896.d:
On this day, in the battle of Charai/ Chahrai/ Charegaum/ Kamorle/ marand janjira was forced upon a surprised siddi sAt; and the evil Siddi sAt was killed by chimnAjI appa's forces the next day.

Events
Chimnaji Appa under took the work seriously.  
Learning that Siddi Sat had left his base at Anjanvel and moved with all his forces threatening Kolaba, the renowned stronghold built by Shivaji, he diverted his course towards the enemy's quarters and suddenly attacked Siddi Sat as he was encamped near Rewas. The latter had no alternative but to face Chimnaji Appa's 3x cavalry in an open sight. A bloody action ensued at the villages of Charegaum and Kamarlen, in which Siddi Sat was killed while defending him self valiantly. More than 1300 of his brave followers were slain, including Siddi Yakut the defender of Underi, and a much larger number wounded. 

No.192 - 2 May 1736 (Gregorian?)
Chimaji writing about the battle of Charai, where the Siddi Sat was killed.

> Siddi Sat, with his full force came to Revas. We attacked and destroyed it. 60 men were in entrenchments, who were killed. Manaji Angre fought a battle. We lost a good officer. (Not Manaji). 2 more engagements were fought. 50-55 men fell on our side among Angre's forces. The Habshi's province was captured and pillaged. 
> 
> He planned to attack Rajkot. Rajashri Sambhaji Angre was already deployed against him. As soon as Rajashri Angre's letter arrived, we immediately marched fast and intercepted his force near Poyna. 
> 
> On the next day, Siddi Sat with his handpicked forces of around 1500 came to the village of Charai. We deployed our men. The Siddis are a brave people. They endured our firepower and came at us boldly. We lost many men and horses, but with the Swami's blessings, the Siddi Sat was killed. Among his officers, Davkod Naik, Subanji Ghatga, Faim, and Balaji Shenvi were killed. We killed some 1200 to 1300 of his soldiers. Rajashri Angre also reached the battlefield in time. His men also joined in the fray, as I have written earlier. Krishnaji Ghatga's death was written about, earlier, but Krishnaji Bodke escaped. The remaining sardars and jematdars were also killed. His son also escaped by diving into the river and swimming away. The Habshis have taken a major setback.

Context
siddi sAt, a competent admiral, was an evil Islamist. He had on shivarAtri day of 1727, surprised the celebrations, demolished the parashurAma temple in chiplun and tortrued + killed several brAhmaNa-s, rousing the ire of svAmI brahmendra and much of marAThas.

Aftermath
This signal victory over the implacable Siddi who had destroyed the famous Hindu shrine of Parashuram, roused all Maharashtra to heights of ecstasy and carned an imperishable fame for Chimnaji Appa. There was great jubiliation in the marATha capital.

Saying 

> “By killing Siddi Sat, a demon of the type of Ravana, you have uprooted the very life of the Siddis and earned an undying fame."  

Shahu showered upon Chimnaji honours, costly ornaments and dresses, including a sword set with diamonds. The event naturally unnerved the Siddis of Janjira and induced them to seek a humiliating peace with the Peshwa. Anjanvel and Govalkot alone remained as their mainland posts, and came to be captured much later by Tulaji Angria in January 1745, so that Brahmendra Swami could have a happy death in 1746 after seeing his wrongs fully avenged.

70d24916b4.d: Son of Śrī Acyutaśarmā of Koṅkaṇadeśa, having offered his services of preparing sandal paste for the worship of Śrī Chandramoulīśvara, He was offered kingship of Kashmir by King Harṣa for his poetical wisdom/merits. Having ruled Kashmir for a short period, He came back to his preceptor Arbhakaśaṅkara and got initiated into asceticism with the name Sārvabhauma Chandracūḍendra Sarasvatī. Preceptor Śrī Chandracūḍendra Sarasvatī leading for ten years a pious life on the banks of Ganges, establishing on his throne revered Madhura the incarnation of Dhanvantari and adorning him with the title Paripūrṇabodha reached/attained his Bhagavan’s immortal abode on the night of Kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī in the year Vijaya.

7104ff3beb.d:
The Krishna-paksha Ekadashi of phālguna month is known as pāpamōchanī-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
7104ff3beb.s:
𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌯𑌦𑍀𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌃।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍁𑌭𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌿॥  
  
𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰।  
𑌭𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑌥𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍇 𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌵 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵।  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍋 𑌨 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
--𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇  
  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑍈𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑍌𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑍋𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇।  
𑌸 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌕𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌗𑌦𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩௫॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥௩௬॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌕𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌚𑍋𑌦𑌕𑌂 𑌪𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௩௮॥  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥 𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍀।  
𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௯॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍋 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍇 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃॥௪௦॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌗𑍋𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌪𑌾𑌰𑌗𑍇॥௪௧॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍋 𑌯𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌕𑌾𑌃॥௪௩॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌏𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௪௪॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௧௮॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌮𑍁𑌰𑌵𑌧𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥௪௦॥

7116965022.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and budhaḥ in puṣyaḥ karkaṭaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°33′09.56″.
7116965022.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°33′09.56″, 0°32′51.41″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at puṣyaḥ-4 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 0°29′56.69″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.79, elongation 12°31′25.66″ W). budhaḥ at puṣyaḥ-4 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°03′06.25″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.26, elongation 12°33′26.96″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

716e23b5ad.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in uttaraprōṣṭhapadā mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°54′42.92″.
716e23b5ad.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°54′42.92″, 0°54′30.15″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°07′32.63″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.97, elongation 14°48′02.45″ E). śukraḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°12′49.71″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 14°41′58.87″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

71f2c1eb2d.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and śukraḥ in mūlā dhanuḥ, center-to-center separation 0°18′37.86″.
71f2c1eb2d.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°18′37.86″, 0°18′30.03″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at mūlā-2 dhanuḥ (latitude 1°00′03.81″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.28, elongation 26°56′19.64″ E). śukraḥ at mūlā-2 dhanuḥ (latitude 1°18′41.67″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 26°57′03.98″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śukraḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

722d3415aa.d: Major Mohit Sharma, SM (who'd earlier, in the guise of angry young Kashmiri Iftikaar Bhatt had infiltrated Hizbul Mujahideen, dramatically killed jihAdi commanders Abu Sabjar and Abu Torara and escaped), was leading Bravo Assault Team in operations in Kupwara District of North Kashmir. ... terrorists fired from three directions indiscriminately. In the heavy exchange of fire, four commandos were wounded immediately. With complete disregard to his safety, he crawled and recovered two soldiers to safety. Unmindful of the overwhelming fire, he threw grenades and killed two terrorists but was shot in the chest. In the brief respite that followed, he kept directing his commandos, in spite of serious injuries. Sensing further danger to his comrades, he charged in a daring close quarter combat killing two more terrorists. His last words to his 2nd in command was, "Make sure not one escapes the net."

723e1f53a2.d:
The Krishna-paksha Ekadashi of śrāvaṇa month is known as ajā-ēkādaśī. Satya Harishchandra performed this to get back family and kingdom.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
723e1f53a2.s:
𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌯𑌦𑍀𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌃।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍁𑌭𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌿॥  
  
𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰।  
𑌭𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑌥𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍇 𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌵 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵।  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍋 𑌨 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
--𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇  
  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑍈𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑍌𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑍋𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇।  
𑌸 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌕𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌗𑌦𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩௫॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥௩௬॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌕𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌚𑍋𑌦𑌕𑌂 𑌪𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௩௮॥  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥 𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍀।  
𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௯॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍋 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍇 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃॥௪௦॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌗𑍋𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌪𑌾𑌰𑌗𑍇॥௪௧॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍋 𑌯𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌕𑌾𑌃॥௪௩॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌏𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௪௪॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௧௮॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌮𑍁𑌰𑌵𑌧𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥௪௦॥

72598b7f98.d: Umbral magnitude: 0.07 (parimāṇa ≈0.8 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 12:06►01:18 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra ārdrā/punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or viśākhā (anujanma) or pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: mithunam, karkaṭaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ get more ashubha phala, tulā, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ somewhat ashubha, siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, mēṣaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°18′37.57″, 0°18′29.74″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at mūlā-2 dhanuḥ (latitude 1°00′03.28″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.28, elongation 26°56′18.92″ E). śukraḥ at mūlā-2 dhanuḥ (latitude 1°18′40.85″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 26°57′03.26″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śukraḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

73630c291f.d:
Dvadashi tithi, which is followed by an amāvāsyā or paurṇamāsī that touches two consecutive days at sunrise. When either the new moon or the full moon lasts for the entire day and night with sixty ghaṭikās and extends into the day of pratipad (the first day of the next fortnight), it is known as Pakṣavardhinī, which is ‘equivalent’ to myriads of horse sacrifices. Those wise individuals who have learned about the greatness of Pakṣavardhinī have accumulated meritorious deeds until the end of time. By keeping awake in honour of Bhagavan Viṣṇu, one attains the religious merit equivalent to practicing the Pañcāgnisādhana or visiting sacred places. Pakṣavardhinī is virtuous, pure, and destroys sins. Fasting on Pakṣavardhinī eradicates the sins equivalent to crores of brahmahatyā-s.

O sage, it was once observed by Vasiṣṭha and Bhāradvāja, and it is cherished by Bhagavan Viṣṇu and observed by Dhruva and Ambarīṣa. Pakṣavardhinī is as virtuous as Kāśī and as sacred as Dvārakā. Fasting on this day grants a devotee their desired object. It is exceedingly blessed and destroys the sin of tens of thousands of hatyā-s. It should be especially observed by those devoted to knowledge. Bhagavan Sarveshvara should be served by all who are committed to observing this vow. As the moon waxes, especially during the bright half, so does the merit of Pakṣavardhinī increase for the devotee of Bhagavan Viṣṇu. Just as darkness dissipates at sunrise, the sins of a person observing the vow of Pakṣavardhinī vanish.

𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌿𑌕𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌨𑍀।  
𑌉𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌨𑍀॥௨௬॥  
𑌵𑌸𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇𑌨 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌜𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍈 𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍇।

𑌉𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌚 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌛𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌚 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍌॥௨௮॥  
𑌇𑌯𑌂 𑌧𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌧𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌮𑌾 𑌹𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌨𑍀।  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑍇𑌣 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌰𑍈𑌃॥௨௯॥

𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌚 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌤𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌨𑍀॥௩௧॥  
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌯𑍇 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌧𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑌾𑌦𑌪𑌿।

7365ac5c4f.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and śukraḥ in pūrvāṣāḍhā dhanuḥ, center-to-center separation 0°10′25.60″.
7365ac5c4f.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°10′25.60″, 0°10′18.78″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°56′03.48″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.08, elongation 0°59′32.61″ E). śukraḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°45′37.88″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 0°49′52.31″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here aṅgārakaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

On 22nd August 1922, Alluri Sitarama Raju's tribal army initiated their struggle by raiding three police stations Chintapalli Police Station, Krishnadevipeta Police Station, and Rajavommangi on three consecutive days. After the raids they captured a huge number of guns, bayonets and cartridges and swords.

Context
24 year old Alluri Sitarama Raju was a young hindu sannyAsI who gained popularity amongst the Andhra tribals, and motivated their struggle against their social ills, Christian missionaries and the British.

739e419455.b: Observed on Śukla-Ṣaṣṭhī tithi of Āṣāḍhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
739e419455.d:
The temple of Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy, which has been a center of devotion from ancient times, once fell into disrepair. It was later renovated by Chinna Tirumalacharya, the grandson of Sri Tallapaka Annamacharya, as evidenced by an inscription dated March 22nd, 1510 CE at the temple's entrance. Despite regaining its glory for several years, the temple again faced neglect in the 20th century.

In 1940, an Archaka named Sri Sundara Raja Swamy from Kanchi, inspired by a dream in which Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy appeared, took it upon himself to clean the temple premises and resume regular pujas. He conveyed his dream to the villagers, narrating how Shri Venkateshwara Swamy manifested in the dream and instructed him to restore the temple's former splendor (Past Vaibhavam) by conducting Deepa Naivedya Aaradhana, after which Bhagavan vanished from the dream. On July 11, 1940, which was Ashada Shukla Paksha Shashti, Sundara Raja Swamy conducted a special puja, marking the day the deity revealed his divine form to devotees. This event led the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams to initiate the annual “Sakshatkara Vaibhavotsavams.”

“Sakshatkaram” refers to the deity's holy appearance or Darshan. The Sakshatkara Vaibhavotsavam is a three-day festival that includes the day of the deity’s appearance (Ashada Suddha Shasti) and the days immediately before and after. The first day of the celebration includes a procession of the deity, Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy, along with His consorts, on the Pedda Shesha Vahanam, from the temple to the Kalyana Mandapa, followed by Abhishekam and Unjal Seva in the evening. The second day features Hanumantha Vahana Seva, and the third day concludes with the Garuda Vahana Seva at night. These celebrations provide devotees the opportunity to witness the deity and receive blessings.

73cc5f9cab.b: Observed on Śukla-Caturdaśī tithi of every (lunar) month (Sāṅgavaḥ/paraviddha).
73cc5f9cab.d: Anadhyayana on account of chaturdaśī. Several tithis in a month are nitya-anadhyayana days, including prathamā, aṣṭamī, chaturdaśī, amāvāsyā and pūrṇimā. Manu has said that performing adhyayana on these days destroys the Guru (Amavasya), Shishya (Chaturdashi) and the vīrya of the brahma (vēda) itself (Ashtami/Purnima). Similarly, Jabali Rishi has said that Adhyayana on prathama hurts the buddhi while adhyayana on chaturdaśī hurts the brahma (vēda) itself!

𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿॥  
𑌯𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌃—

This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°30′36.02″, 0°30′28.71″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at āśrēṣā-3 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°44′30.81″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -2.04, elongation 1°45′13.87″ W). śukraḥ at āśrēṣā-3 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°13′54.79″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 1°14′55.65″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

7441d453b4.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈0.9 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
7441d453b4.d: Magnitude: 7% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈0.9 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 02:50►17:12 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
7441d453b4.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

747e805c21.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°10′25.82″, 0°10′18.99″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°56′02.94″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.08, elongation 0°59′33.03″ E). śukraḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°45′37.12″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 0°49′52.47″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here aṅgārakaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
747e805c21.s:

748715ca65.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈9.6 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
748715ca65.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.80 (parimāṇa ≈9.6 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:23►20:08 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

74a5a794bd.d: It is said in Vishnu Purāṇam that when Amavasya overlaps with one of nine nakshatras---Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati, Pushya, Ardra, Punarvasu, Shravishtha, Purvaproshthapada, or Shatabhishak---it is sacred even for Devas. For instance, Shraaddha done on an Amavasya joined with Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati keeps the pitrs satisfied for eight years. Likewise, on Pushya, Ardra and Punarvasu, the pitrs are satisfied for twelve years. It is said in the Smrtis, that if Amavasya falls on a Monday, Tuesday or Thursday, such a tithi is given the appellation puṣkalā and is as sacred as a solar eclipse. amāvāsyā of jyaiṣṭha lunar month.

𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌂 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌵𑌾𑌜𑍈𑌕𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍃𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌿𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌾।  
𑌨𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍃𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌵𑌨𑍀𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---

74ff6a15a2.s:
𑌅𑌧𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌪𑌿𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌦𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇॥  
𑌸𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌮𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌅𑌧𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮।  
𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌛𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌅𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌵।  
𑌤𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍁𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌤𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍁𑌲𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃।  
𑌆𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿 𑌮𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌲𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌦𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌅𑌧𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌉𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌤𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌨𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌦𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌯 𑌚।  
𑌸𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌚 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌨𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌮𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌵𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍇𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍈𑌷 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌃।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌸𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌮𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌃, 𑌧𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇𑌨 𑌕𑌾𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌿𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍌 𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌭𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌚।  
𑌨 𑌚 𑌨𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌯𑍇-𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌮𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌃।

7505885e48.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and budhaḥ in maghā siṁhaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°37′21.38″.
7505885e48.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°37′21.38″, 0°37′03.83″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°54′42.84″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.70, elongation 8°32′44.06″ E). budhaḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 1°32′04.22″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.11, elongation 8°38′01.24″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
7505885e48.s:

--𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇

7510cc9f1f.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈0.8 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
7510cc9f1f.d: Umbral magnitude: 0.07 (parimāṇa ≈0.8 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 10:09►22:18 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra ārdrā/punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or viśākhā (anujanma) or pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: mithunam, karkaṭaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ get more ashubha phala, tulā, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ somewhat ashubha, siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, mēṣaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
7510cc9f1f.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

752471d9c7.s:
𑌕𑍃𑌪𑌾𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌮𑍁𑌖𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌜𑌟𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑌿-𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌦𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌂 𑌰𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌂 𑌚𑌿𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌰𑍇𑌶𑌂 𑌹𑍃𑌦𑌿 𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿॥

𑌵𑌾𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌦𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌹𑌿𑌮𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌗𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇।  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌂 𑌶𑍀𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌵 𑌕𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌭𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌥 𑌸𑍋𑌢𑍁𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌵 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃

759cd4d3f2.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and budhaḥ in puṣyaḥ karkaṭaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°33′11.47″.
759cd4d3f2.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°33′11.47″, 0°32′53.32″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at puṣyaḥ-4 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 0°29′57.13″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.79, elongation 12°31′24.40″ W). budhaḥ at puṣyaḥ-4 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°03′08.60″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.26, elongation 12°33′25.76″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

75dd7f5128.b: Event occured on 1737-04-08 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
75dd7f5128.d:
A Maratha force commanded by Shankaraji Phadke, Anjurkar, Bajirao Belose, Rayajirao Surve & 400 soldiers caught the Portuguese by surprise and forced them to abandon the fort. The victory was commemorated by a plaque installed on the northern wall of the fort and is still visible today. The Marathas then rebuilt the fort, constructing three bastions Bahirav, Bhavani, and Bava.

Context: In 1737 the then Peshwa Baji Rao I sent his brother, Chimaji Appa, to take the Bassein Fort from the Portuguese. After winning the Battle of Vasai, his general, Shankarji Pant, persuaded Chimaji to launch an assault on Fort Arnala, for its strategic importance to the Maratha navy in assaulting Portuguese interests. Their first assault, coordinated with a Maratha naval force commanded by Manaji Agre, was routed by a superior Portuguese naval force.

760165560e.d:
In an attack (allegedly by  Abdul Hamid Gada of Hizbul Mujahideen = 'Party of Holy Fighters'), timed to coincide with the Shab-e-Qadar, the holiest night of Ramadan, 26 Kashmiri Hindus living in the village of Wandhama were slaughtered.

The gunmen came to their house dressed like Indian Army soldiers, had tea with them, waiting for a radio message indicating that all Hindu families in the village had been covered, lined them up and shot them dead.

Aftermath
Politicians expressed "kaDhI nindA". PM Gujral flew to Kashmir for national winter games at Gulmarg. He inaugurated sports carnival on 28 Jan when smoke & ashes of funeral pyres were still in air.

Gada was subsequently killed in an operation by Indian security forces in 2000.

76954cfc7a.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and śukraḥ in mūlā dhanuḥ, center-to-center separation 0°18′37.14″.
76954cfc7a.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°18′37.14″, 0°18′29.30″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at mūlā-2 dhanuḥ (latitude 1°00′02.46″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.28, elongation 26°56′19.10″ E). śukraḥ at mūlā-2 dhanuḥ (latitude 1°18′39.60″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 26°57′03.43″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śukraḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

---𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌕𑌰𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌾𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌶𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌤𑌪𑌃—  
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।

77b19ec664.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°36′15.00″.
77b19ec664.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°36′15.00″, 0°36′01.59″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°15′32.25″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.71, elongation 25°42′15.30″ W). śukraḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°39′17.25″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.87, elongation 25°39′40.89″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

780cad1e8e.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃---  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌛𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥  
𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍀 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍀 𑌚 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌃।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥  
𑌹𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌆𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---   
𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌤𑌦𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌲𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌲𑌿𑌃।

78ba21f1df.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śaniḥ in uttaraprōṣṭhapadā mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°27′35.56″.
78ba21f1df.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°27′35.56″, 0°27′24.85″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°36′40.74″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -0.17, elongation 22°36′42.37″ W). śaniḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°09′05.18″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.93, elongation 22°33′56.84″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

793a157482.d:
The Shukla-paksha Ekadashi of vaiśākha month is known as mōhinī-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
793a157482.s:
𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌯𑌦𑍀𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌃।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍁𑌭𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌿॥  
  
𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰।  
𑌭𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑌥𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍇 𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌵 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵।  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍋 𑌨 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
--𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇  
  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑍈𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑍌𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑍋𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇।  
𑌸 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌕𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌗𑌦𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩௫॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥௩௬॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌕𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌚𑍋𑌦𑌕𑌂 𑌪𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௩௮॥  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥 𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍀।  
𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௯॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍋 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍇 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃॥௪௦॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌗𑍋𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌪𑌾𑌰𑌗𑍇॥௪௧॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍋 𑌯𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌕𑌾𑌃॥௪௩॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌏𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௪௪॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௧௮॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌮𑍁𑌰𑌵𑌧𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥௪௦॥

796520bfc6.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and śukraḥ in pūrvāṣāḍhā dhanuḥ, center-to-center separation 0°10′25.70″.
796520bfc6.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°10′25.70″, 0°10′18.88″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°56′03.24″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.08, elongation 0°59′32.85″ E). śukraḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°45′37.53″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 0°49′52.43″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here aṅgārakaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

797b43de81.d: The Brahmotsavam of Nataraja at Chidambaram happens specially around the Aani Thirumanjana festival each year, for ten days. On this day, Nataraja gives darshan with a golden ‘surya prabha’ vahanam.

797eccf227.d:
On this day, Maharaja Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma of Travancore issued the  Temple Entry Proclamation.

Context
Kerala is a rare state where caste discrimination actually led to conversion to abrahamist faiths because converts got more rights than low jAti-s. In other states, the primary factor in conversion was and remains selectively targetted allurements, supposed miracles and threats.

Vaikom Satyagraha protests sought equal rights of access in areas previously restricted to members of upper castes. The protests expanded to become a movement seeking rights of access to the interior of the temples themselves. Regent Maharani Sethu Lakshmi Bayi yielded partly - deferring to her minor nephew (who supposedly assured gAndhI on his own will).

Implementation
Chithira Thirunal signed the Proclamation on the eve of his 24th birthday in 1936. He was ably supported by his divAn Sachivottama Sir Chetput Pattabhiraman Ramaswami Iyer, who clarified that the decision was a result of his own free will and not the result of protests or advice; and carefully managed its acceptance and implementation.

Aftermath
 The Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation did not have a serious influence in Cochin or British Malabar as the Maharajah of Cochin and the Zamorin were staunch opponents of temple entry for dalits. Even when universal temple entry was granted in 1947 the Cochin maharajah made an exemption in the bill so as to keep his family temple, "Sree Poornathrayeesha", out of the purview of temple entry.

79e87d5c63.d:
On 11th May 1951, the first President of India Sri Rajendra Prasad ji reopened the ancient Jyotirlinga Kshetram of Somnath in Gujarat. It was reconsecrated after several centuries!

Strong opposition came from Nehru! He didn’t want him to go for this inauguration. But the President was a very determined man of Dharma. He even lead the procession to the temple!

Context
The ancient temple was raided, plundered and looted over 17 times by Muhammad of Ghazni. It was a great source of shame for Hindus. For some time the place came under the control of the Nawab of Junagarh. He wouldn’t allow any reconstruction! After Junagarh joined India in Oct 1947, Patel announced at a public meeting:

> “On this auspicious day of the New Year, we have decided that Somnath should be reconstructed. You, people of Saurashtra, should do your best. This is a holy task in which all should participate!”

79ef2256db.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′13.73″.
79ef2256db.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′13.73″, 0°59′04.07″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′47.62″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.32″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′33.89″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.71″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

7a0f01b5c9.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈6.4 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
7a0f01b5c9.d: Magnitude: 53% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈6.4 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 03:16►17:46 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
7a0f01b5c9.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

7a1b1a892c.d: Mithuna-Ravi-Saṅkramaṇa-Ṣaḍaśīti Punyakala. Perform danam of clothes, food and water. For ṣaḍaśīti-puṇyakāla like mithuna-saṅkramaṇa, the 60 ghatikas succeeding the saṅkramaṇa form a puṇyakāla; in general, the ghatikas closer to the puṇyakāla are even more sacred.
7a1b1a892c.s:
𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌮𑌿𑌥𑍁𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑍁॥  
---𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌕𑌰𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌾𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌶𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌤𑌪𑌃—  
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌸𑍁 𑌰𑍋𑌗𑍀 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍀 𑌚 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌹𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑍈𑌃।  
𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌃 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌸𑍁 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
---𑌵𑍈𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌥-𑌦𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇 𑌆𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌕-𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌃 (𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌃)  
𑌷𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍁𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇।  
𑌦𑍃𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑌾𑌗𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌨𑍈𑌵 𑌦𑍃𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
---𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇

7aa9cf4378.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and budhaḥ in uttarāṣāḍhā makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°57′44.77″.
7aa9cf4378.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°57′44.77″, 0°57′40.46″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-2 makaraḥ (latitude 0°59′14.42″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.08, elongation 2°22′19.72″ W). budhaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-2 makaraḥ (latitude 1°56′59.19″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.24, elongation 2°54′24.86″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

7aaeb2c5e7.b: Event occured on 1706-03-15 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
7aaeb2c5e7.d:
Battle of Ratanpur (near Rajpipla,Gujarat): Marathas crushed Mughals in this battle, inspiring rebellion of Ajit Singh again. Durgadas Rathore left Mughals too (again)!

Context
A letter was sent to the governor of Baroda that he should join the force that was being sent to Surat. These officers advanced as far as the Baba Piara (Bawapir) ford on the Narmada, where they remained encamped for a month and a half in inactivity and quarrels, merely sending out spies to ascertain where the Maratha army was located. At last, stern reproofs from Abdul Hamid Khan compelled them to cross the Narmada and to march forward until they reached the village of Ratanpur on the other side, where they pitched their camps at some distance from each other. Here their scattered armies were surprised by the great Maratha host and their raw levies were routed in two separate engagements. 

Aftermath
Many of Mughal troops the were drowned in the Narbada in their flight, while those who escaped managed with difficulty to make their way to Broach. Safdar Khan Babi was wounded and taken prisoner while Nazar Ali Khan burned his tents and was forced to flee for his life.

7b621305e4.d: Shukla Dvadashi tithi, combined with Rohini nakshatra. Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, and Pāpanāśinī—all these days have the power to destroy sins and should be observed by those seeking specific benefits. When Dvādaśī in the bright half coincides with Rohiṇī, it is called Jayantī. This day also removes sins. Worshipping Viṣṇu on this day undoubtedly cleanses one of all sins, whether small or great, committed during the past seven lifetimes.

7c29c1ce6f.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′08.97″.
7c29c1ce6f.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′08.97″, 0°41′01.61″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′21.54″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′40.23″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′12.56″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′41.12″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
